v2 DEMOTES v1'S TWO-GROUP DISCRIMINATOR FROM A SETTLED SPLIT TO A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT A 36-FUNCTION FLOOR, AND KEEPS EVERYTHING ELSE. This edge exists because v1 has been counter-exampled for a day with no `superseded_by` on it, so `gdlmem laws` still ranks its two-group split as settled -- exactly the failure claim.law.CU_a-correcting-law-published-as-a-new-law-leaves-the-corrected-clause-live-at-equal-rank-and-the-addr16-family-has-one-supersession-edge-in-sixteen.20260904.v1 names.

WHAT IS RETIRED, VERBATIM FROM v1: 'THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE DESTINATION REGISTER, NOT THE HOISTING. Census over 36 functions in 15 TUs at commit 71de6e8e7 ... ELEVEN functions emit an ADDR16_LO before the `stwu`, and they split cleanly in two. FOUR write it into r0 and every one of those owes the `mr` ... SEVEN write it into a NAMED volatile and none of them owes a copy, because those values are consumed as call arguments or temps rather than parked in a web.' THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE, and it is v1's OWN named falsifier discharged verbatim ('a re-run of the census below in which the r0-versus-named-volatile discriminator fails to separate the two groups'): claim.law.CR_the-pre-frame-addr16lo-r0-versus-named-volatile-discriminator-has-a-counter-example-and-the-census-floor-is-the-reason.20260904.v1 exhibits game/enemy/critter::ProcessCritterList as a TWELFTH pre-frame instance that writes into a NAMED VOLATILE and OWES THE COPY -- ours `@0x10 addi r4,r4,0 @gPlayers(ADDR16_LO)` before the frame-opening `@0x18 stwu r1,-24(r1)`, then paying `@0x1c addi r5,r4,0`, against the target's single `@0x1c addi r5,r3,0 @gPlayers(ADDR16_LO)`, counts 50/49. So the destination register is NOT the carrier. THE SURVIVING CANDIDATE DISTINCTION, and v2 states it as a candidate rather than a replacement discriminator: whether the value is PARKED IN A WEB or CONSUMED AS A CALL ARGUMENT -- ProcessCritterList's copy destination r5 and its source r4 are both volatile, so register identity cannot be doing the work.

WHY v1 MISSED IT IS NOT AN AUTHORSHIP ERROR, and v2 preserves the distinction: v1's own closing sentence says the population 'is a floor over 36 screened functions and not an image-wide total'. game/enemy/critter was not among the 36. A discriminator derived from a floor is a hypothesis about the floor; the error was in later READINGS of the two-group split as settled, which is precisely what an unmarked correcting law invites.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED AND IS STRENGTHENED. (a) THE r0 HALF IS UNCHALLENGED: where ours completes the ADDR16_LO before the `stwu` into r0, a copy is owed, and no counter-example exists. (b) THE RESIDUAL SHAPE: exactly one surplus `mr`/`addi`, count-asymmetric by one, `fndiff --ops` signature `insert T[3:3]@c-c=[] O[3:4]@c-10=['addi']` plus `replace T[..]=['addi'] O[..]=['mr'] [SHIFTABLE]`, and the postprocessor path is barred by claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-a-count-asymmetric-residual.20260831.v1. (c) THE NEGATIVE LEVERS, all three of which the counter-example CONFIRMS rather than disturbs: declaration order is categorically dead on a member (NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL on dcsReadCalls), `#pragma opt_propagation off` is not the cause, and declaration-with-initialiser versus body-assignment is a proved boundary; the only lever measured to move such a prologue is a CROSS-CLASS declaration exchange. ProcessCritterList has one address-class local and three int-class locals, so no cross-class exchange exists there, and three declaration orders left the copy and the 50/49 count untouched -- v1's disposition predicting exactly this, on a function it did not know about. DO NOT SPEND PROBES on declaration order, declaration form, or opt_propagation on any member.

THE FALSIFIER v1 SHIPPED CANNOT BE RUN BY ANYONE, AND THAT IS A SEPARATE DEFECT THIS RECORD MUST NOT PAPER OVER. v1 names its census as `NC_scratch/nc_prologue_census.py`, an untracked per-worktree path.
